interventions.z: MAGE binds intent into drift-checked models — the spec is not a document but an enforced, executable model the environment holds implementation to.

interventions.x: Deciding who does what in a software project has long been an organizational, human concern.
interventions.y: The field is beginning to treat governance of agentic software engineering as a first-class, formalizable subject — Ait et al. propose a domain-specific language for defining and enforcing governance policies across mixed human-agent teams.
interventions.z: MAGE converges with that direction but works at a different grain: not a single policy language, but a repertoire of governance mechanisms grounded in a production case.

interventions.title: The new measurement regime / commoditized intelligence
interventions.x: Empirical software engineering has long tried to measure process interventions whose effects were small beside the variation among developers — skill, context, and intelligence swamped the signal.
interventions.y: GenAI commoditizes the intelligence input: a ~400-study systematic review maps the field's effort, a three-firm field experiment across 4,867 developers measures a 26% rise in completed tasks, and the canonical single-task RCT clocks a 55.8% speedup — with honest complications where experienced developers in familiar repositories slow down.
interventions.z: MAGE proposes to hold the intelligence confound fixed and vary the environment, representations, and governance — a measurement regime whose effects are large and reproducible enough to build cumulative theory on.
interventions.notes: Registers the S2 empirical-SE-decades claim + closes the measurement-regime LPP gap (cites landed in prose in publish #2 but modeled nowhere). hou2024llm4se situates the 'hundreds of studies / decades of effort' framing (a ~400-study SLR); cui2025genai + peng2023copilot substantiate the controlled gains; metr2025productivity situates the 'if modest, sometimes reverses' hedge (16 devs, 19% slower in familiar repos). interventions.title: Capability model, not a maturity ladder
interventions.x: For two decades the staged software maturity model — the CMM and its CMMI successor — was the dominant frame for engineering quality: rank an organization on a five-rung ladder and tell it to climb.
interventions.y: The staged model drew a documented critique — software capability evaluations grade process conformance in place of the outcomes the process was meant to produce, and under pressure the ladder decays into box-ticking (Bollinger & McGowan).
interventions.z: MAGE is a capability model, not a maturity ladder: a project's current bottleneck selects the next modeling or governance capability it needs, so no rung becomes the goal.
interventions.notes: Registers + backs the S3 CMM box-ticking claim (6.0:229) per the author's CITE ruling. Bollinger & McGowan, 'A Critical Look at Software Capability Evaluations', IEEE Software 8(4):25-41, 1991 (DOI 10.1109/52.300034; IEEE Software 25th-anniversary Top Pick) documents the process-conformance-over-outcomes + box-ticking failure mode — relation=substantiates. backs_claims binds the DISCUSSION claim maturity-model-box-ticking (registered in discussion-claims.json). The cite marker [cite: bollinger1991critical] is in 6.0 prose at the box-ticking sentence. interventions.title: Agile as an accidental-complexity concession
interventions.x: Agile's founding statement chose velocity over ceremony — it valued working software over comprehensive documentation and responding to change over following a plan, deprioritizing the up-front models and maintained plans that heavier methodologies demanded.
interventions.y: This book reads that observable choice as an accidental-complexity concession: teams shipped fast and kept models thin because holding quality and a current model honest by hand was too expensive to afford at pace — an owned causal-historical interpretation, not an established finding.
interventions.z: MAGE changes that arithmetic: agents absorb the accidental work — they type the code, keep the map in sync, and hold the line for cents — so the essential properties a model names and a gate checks can finally get the attention Agile had to spend elsewhere.
interventions.notes: Registers the S1 Agile-origin claim (6.1:365-368) per the author's HYBRID ruling. The Agile Manifesto (agile-manifesto2001; Beck et al., 'Manifesto for Agile Software Development', 2001, agilemanifesto.org) grounds the OBSERVABLE half — Agile's 'working software over comprehensive documentation' + 'responding to change over following a plan' values ARE the documentation/model concession the passage describes — relation=situates (it documents the choice, it does not establish the author's causal reading). The CAUSAL half (arose BECAUSE hand-maintenance was too expensive at pace) is the author's owned interpretation, registered in discussion-claims.json with frame=conjecture and kept loud in prose (no softening). backs_claims + advances_theses bind the DISCUSSION claim agile-accidental-complexity-origin.
